subject: System Design
title: What Is a Monolith
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Is a Monolith.

hook.text: Every feature, every module, every line of code lives in one deployable unit. That's a monolith.

buildup.text: A monolithic application ships as a single binary or package. All components share the same process and memory.

discovery.text: Monoliths are simple to develop, test, and deploy. One build, one deploy, one running process.

twist.text: As the codebase grows, teams step on each other. A bug in one module can crash the entire application.

climax.text: Monoliths aren't bad — they're the simplest starting point. Most successful companies started with one.

punchline.text: One codebase, one deploy — simple until it isn't.

quiz.question: What is a monolithic application?
options: A single deployable unit containing all features
